name: Meta-Labelled Primary Signal
note: Lopez de Prado meta-labelling. The primary (a 20/50 EMA cross, standing in for any of the existing families) sets the side; every primary signal is labelled by its own triple-barrier outcome (+tp*sigma, -sl*sigma, vertical at `vert` bars, sigma = EWM sd of log returns span 50); a logistic secondary is trained online on [ADX, ATR/mean(ATR,100), (C-EMA50)/ATR, ln(V/mean(V,20)), RSI, permutation entropy d=3 over 40 returns, hours since the cash open], using ONLY labels whose vertical barrier has closed plus an embargo. A signal is taken only when the secondary's probability clears the cut, and the exit is the same three barriers the label used, honoured through exit_signal plus a time_stop. ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE: the published cut of 0.55 is applied as a lift over the training base rate, cut = 2*base*thresh, which is exactly p > thresh when the labels are balanced. Measured on real bars the triple-barrier base rate is 0.35 on SPY and 0.18 on XLU under the 2:1 barrier, so a fixed 0.55 takes 10% of SPY signals and none at all of XLU's -- an absolute cut is not comparable across symbols or across barrier settings, and the family would be dead on most of its own grid. Not implemented: probability-proportional sizing, because size belongs to the shared runner. Note the exec grid can override tp_atr/st_atr and add a second, ATR-based exit on top of the barriers.
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (Wiley, 2018), Ch. 3 (triple-barrier labelling, getEvents/getBins) and section 3.6 (meta-labelling); purging and embargo from Ch. 7. Empirical evaluation: Hudson & Thames, 'Does Meta Labeling Add to Signal Efficacy?'.
code:
_PERM = {(0, 1, 2): 0, (0, 2, 1): 1, (1, 0, 2): 2,
         (1, 2, 0): 3, (2, 0, 1): 4, (2, 1, 0): 5}


def family_init(ctx):
    """Meta-labelling: the primary picks the SIDE, a secondary model decides
    whether to take it at all.

    Labels are the primary signal's own triple-barrier outcome -- 1 if the
    +tp*sigma barrier is touched before the -sl*sigma barrier or the vertical
    one, else 0 -- so the secondary is learning when the primary's precision
    is acceptable, not what the market will do.  Only labels whose vertical
    barrier has already closed, plus an embargo, are ever trained on, which is
    the purge that stops overlapping labels leaking.
    """
    import math

    n = len(ctx.bars)
    c = [b["c"] for b in ctx.bars]
    v = [float(b.get("v") or 0.0) for b in ctx.bars]

    ctx.f = ctx.indicator("ema", period=max(2, int(ctx.p.fast)))
    ctx.s = ctx.indicator("ema", period=max(3, int(ctx.p.slow)))
    ctx.adx = ctx.indicator("adx", period=14)
    ctx.atr = ctx.indicator("atr", period=14)
    ctx.rsi = ctx.indicator("rsi", period=14)
    ctx.e50 = ctx.indicator("ema", period=50)

    # ---- EWM sd of log returns, span 50: the barrier unit ----
    lr = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        if c[i] > 0 and c[i - 1] > 0:
            lr[i] = math.log(c[i] / c[i - 1])
    al = 2.0 / (float(ctx.p.span) + 1.0)
    sg = [None] * n
    ev = None
    for i in range(1, n):
        ev = lr[i] * lr[i] if ev is None else al * lr[i] * lr[i] + (1 - al) * ev
        if i >= 30:
            sg[i] = math.sqrt(ev) if ev > 0 else None
    ctx.sg = ctx.series(sg, "ewm_sd")

    # ---- permutation entropy, d = 3, over the last pe_win returns ----
    pw = max(10, int(ctx.p.pe_win))
    pat = [None] * n
    for i in range(3, n):
        vals = (lr[i - 2], lr[i - 1], lr[i])
        order = tuple(sorted(range(3), key=lambda k: vals[k]))
        pat[i] = _PERM[order]
    pe = [None] * n
    cnts = [0] * 6
    buf = []
    for i in range(n):
        p = pat[i]
        if p is None:
            continue
        buf.append(p)
        cnts[p] += 1
        if len(buf) > pw:
            cnts[buf.pop(0)] -= 1
        if len(buf) == pw:
            h = 0.0
            for q in cnts:
                if q:
                    pr = q / float(pw)
                    h -= pr * math.log(pr)
            pe[i] = h / math.log(6.0)
    ctx.pe = ctx.series(pe, "perm_entropy")

    # ---- slow scalers for two of the features ----
    aw = 100
    vw = 20
    vmean = [None] * n
    sv = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        sv += v[i]
        if i >= vw:
            sv -= v[i - vw]
        if i >= vw - 1:
            vmean[i] = sv / vw
    ctx.vmean = ctx.series(vmean, "vol_mean")

    # minutes since the 13:30Z cash open (negative before it). Read off the raw
    # bar dict, since ctx.t is not indexable during init.
    mo = [None] * n
    for i in range(n):
        t = str(ctx.bars[i]["t"])
        try:
            hh = int(t[11:13])
            mm = int(t[14:16])
            mo[i] = (hh * 60 + mm - 810) / 60.0
        except Exception:
            mo[i] = 0.0
    ctx.mo = ctx.series(mo, "hours_since_open")

    # rolling mean of ATR, for the ATR/mean(ATR,100) feature. It is advanced
    # at the top of signal(), which runs on EVERY bar -- doing it inside
    # _feats would average the last 100 SIGNAL bars instead of the last 100
    # bars, which is a different and much slower-moving quantity.
    ctx.aw = aw
    ctx.abuf = []
    ctx.atot = 0.0

    # ---- secondary model state ----
    ctx.K = 7
    ctx.w = [0.0] * ctx.K
    ctx.b0 = 0.0
    ctx.mu = [0.0] * ctx.K
    ctx.sd = [1.0] * ctx.K
    ctx.trained = False
    ctx.base = 0.0
    ctx.open_ev = []          # events whose barriers have not resolved yet
    ctx.samp = []             # (feats, label, ready_at)
    ctx.ready = 0
    ctx.fitted_at = 0
    ctx.last = None           # (dir, profit-take, stop) for the live exit
    ctx.p.time_stop = int(ctx.p.vert)


def _feats(ctx, i):
    a = ctx.atr[i]
    if a is None or a <= 0 or not ctx.abuf:
        return None
    am = ctx.atot / len(ctx.abuf)
    dx = ctx.adx.adx[i]
    rs = ctx.rsi[i]
    e5 = ctx.e50[i]
    vm = ctx.vmean[i]
    pe = ctx.pe[i]
    mo = ctx.mo[i]
    if None in (dx, rs, e5, vm, pe, mo) or am <= 0 or vm <= 0:
        return None
    import math
    vv = ctx.v[i]
    return [dx, a / am, (ctx.c[i] - e5) / a,
            math.log(max(vv, 1.0) / vm), rs, pe, mo]


def _fit(ctx):
    """Logistic regression by full-batch gradient descent, warm started."""
    import math
    K = ctx.K
    rows = ctx.samp[:ctx.ready]
    if len(rows) > int(ctx.p.max_samp):
        rows = rows[-int(ctx.p.max_samp):]
    m = len(rows)
    if m < int(ctx.p.min_train):
        return
    mu = [0.0] * K
    for f, y, _ in rows:
        for k in range(K):
            mu[k] += f[k]
    for k in range(K):
        mu[k] /= m
    sd = [0.0] * K
    for f, y, _ in rows:
        for k in range(K):
            d = f[k] - mu[k]
            sd[k] += d * d
    for k in range(K):
        sd[k] = math.sqrt(sd[k] / m) or 1.0
    ctx.mu, ctx.sd = mu, sd
    X = [[(f[k] - mu[k]) / sd[k] for k in range(K)] for f, y, _ in rows]
    Y = [y for _, y, _ in rows]
    w = list(ctx.w)
    b = ctx.b0
    lr = float(ctx.p.lr)
    l2 = float(ctx.p.l2)
    for _ in range(int(ctx.p.epochs)):
        gw = [0.0] * K
        gb = 0.0
        for r in range(m):
            zsum = b
            xr = X[r]
            for k in range(K):
                zsum += w[k] * xr[k]
            if zsum > 30.0:
                pr = 1.0
            elif zsum < -30.0:
                pr = 0.0
            else:
                pr = 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-zsum))
            e = pr - Y[r]
            gb += e
            for k in range(K):
                gw[k] += e * xr[k]
        for k in range(K):
            w[k] -= lr * (gw[k] / m + l2 * w[k])
        b -= lr * gb / m
    ctx.w, ctx.b0 = w, b
    # the label base rate is a property of the BARRIERS and the symbol, not of
    # the model: it runs 0.18 on XLU and 0.35 on SPY under a 2:1 barrier. The
    # published cut of 0.55 assumes balanced labels, so it is applied as a lift
    # over the base rate -- 2*base*thresh, which IS p > thresh when base = 0.5.
    ctx.base = sum(Y) / float(m)
    ctx.trained = True
    ctx.fitted_at = ctx.ready


def _prob(ctx, f):
    import math
    z = ctx.b0
    for k in range(ctx.K):
        z += ctx.w[k] * (f[k] - ctx.mu[k]) / ctx.sd[k]
    if z > 30.0:
        return 1.0
    if z < -30.0:
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-z))


def signal(ctx, i):
    # ---- 0. advance the 100-bar ATR mean; this runs on every bar ----
    _a = ctx.atr[i]
    if _a is not None and _a > 0:
        ctx.abuf.append(_a)
        ctx.atot += _a
        if len(ctx.abuf) > ctx.aw:
            ctx.atot -= ctx.abuf.pop(0)

    # ---- 1. advance every open event towards its barriers ----
    hi, lo = ctx.h[i], ctx.l[i]
    still = []
    for ev in ctx.open_ev:
        if i <= ev[0]:
            still.append(ev)
            continue
        j, d, f, pt, sl, dead = ev
        lab = None
        if d > 0:
            if lo <= sl:
                lab = 0                 # a bar touching both resolves as the stop
            elif hi >= pt:
                lab = 1
        else:
            if hi >= sl:
                lab = 0
            elif lo <= pt:
                lab = 1
        if lab is None and i >= dead:
            lab = 0                     # vertical barrier: not a profit-take
        if lab is None:
            still.append(ev)
        else:
            ctx.samp.append((f, lab, max(i, dead) + int(ctx.p.embargo)))
    ctx.open_ev = still

    # ---- 2. purge + embargo: which samples may be trained on yet ----
    while ctx.ready < len(ctx.samp) and ctx.samp[ctx.ready][2] <= i:
        ctx.ready += 1
    if ctx.ready - ctx.fitted_at >= int(ctx.p.refit_n):
        _fit(ctx)

    # ---- 3. the primary model ----
    f_, s_ = ctx.f[i], ctx.s[i]
    pf, ps = ctx.f[i - 1], ctx.s[i - 1]
    if None in (f_, s_, pf, ps):
        return 0
    side = 0
    if pf <= ps and f_ > s_:
        side = 1
    elif pf >= ps and f_ < s_:
        side = -1
    if not side:
        return 0

    sg = ctx.sg[i]
    ft = _feats(ctx, i)
    if sg is None or sg <= 0 or ft is None:
        return 0

    px = ctx.c[i]
    pt = px * (1.0 + side * float(ctx.p.tp_mult) * sg)
    sl = px * (1.0 - side * float(ctx.p.sl_mult) * sg)
    # every primary signal becomes a training label, taken or not
    ctx.open_ev.append((i, side, ft, pt, sl, i + int(ctx.p.vert)))

    # ---- 4. the secondary model decides whether to act on it ----
    if not ctx.trained or ctx.base <= 0.0:
        return side if int(ctx.p.warmup_take) else 0
    cut = 2.0 * ctx.base * float(ctx.p.thresh)
    if cut > 0.95:
        cut = 0.95
    if _prob(ctx, ft) <= cut:
        return 0
    ctx.last = (side, pt, sl)
    return side


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Exit on the SAME barriers the label was built from -- anything else
    asks the secondary model a different question than it was trained on."""
    if ctx.last is None or not ctx.positions:
        return False
    d, pt, sl = ctx.last
    if (1 if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long" else -1) != d:
        return False
    if d > 0:
        return ctx.l[i] <= sl or ctx.h[i] >= pt
    return ctx.h[i] >= sl or ctx.l[i] <= pt
